title: Every automated test record gets an outcome, and one that did not run is failed with did not run
when: With a fixture repository whose spec has three automated test records and one that is not automated yet, and suites' output in which two of the automated tests ran: assure record runs at the commit checked out.
then: It exits 0, and the predicate holds one outcome for each automated test record, in ID order. The test that did not run is failed with the detail did not run. The record that is not automated yet has no outcome.

title: Outcomes come from Go and Python subtests by the ID in their names, and a test with no ID is ignored
when: The Python runner runs a suite with a passing subtest that carries an ID and a failing subtest that carries none. The go test -json output has a passing and a failing subtest with IDs, and a failing subtest with no ID. assure record reads both.
then: The outcome of each automated test record is that of the subtest that carries its ID: passed, failed and passed. The failing tests with no ID give no outcome and do not refuse the run.

title: An outcome for an ID that is not a test record refuses the run, and no predicate is written
when: assure record reads go test -json output with a subtest that carries an ID that is not a test record in the spec at the commit.
then: It exits non-zero, names the ID, and writes no predicate and no step output.

title: The subject is the full commit checked out, and a short ID, a branch or another commit is refused
when: With a fixture repository at its second commit: assure record runs with a short ID, with the name of the branch checked out, with the first commit, and then with the full commit checked out. The attest job's subject step of proof-run.yml runs for that commit.
then: The first three runs exit non-zero and write nothing. The last writes a predicate about the commit checked out, and the subject step names that commit as the subject, with the SHA-256 of its ID as the digest.

title: A tree with uncommitted changes is refused, also when git status hides them
when: assure record runs in fixture repositories with a changed file, a staged change, an untracked file, a change hidden by skip-worktree, an automated test record added to the spec and hidden by assume-unchanged, an untracked file hidden by info/exclude, an untracked file hidden by the user's excludes file, another commit's tree shown by a replace ref, a same-size change hidden by minimal stat checks, and a new file hidden by an untracked .gitignore that ignores itself. Each hidden case first shows that git status shows no change.
then: Each run exits non-zero, says that the tree has uncommitted changes, and writes nothing.

title: Only the trusted workflow's attestation job signs the proof run, it runs no repository code, and CI commits no evidence file
when: Reads the proof-run.yml workflow, and reads it key by key: the workflow, and the attest job with every key and every step with each of its keys and values, in order, against the keys, steps and values allowed. Runs its subject step with a branch name, and its predicate check step with a predicate about the commit and with one about another commit. Then assure record runs as a job of another workflow, and then with a predicate file in the repository.
then: The workflow and its suites job may only read the repository, and the workflow has only its allowed keys and no environment but the commit and the Lathe pin. Of the jobs that sign a proof run, only the attest job may write an identity token and attestations. The attest job is exactly: needs the suites job, may only get an identity token and write attestations, has no condition, container or defaults, and its four steps: download the proof run, check that it is about the commit, name the commit as the subject, and sign it with actions/attest at the proof run predicate type with the subject that the subject step names; it checks out and runs no code of the repository. Every action is pinned to a commit, and no step commits or pushes. The suites job checks out the pull request head or the commit pushed and records the proof run at it, under the runner's temporary folder. The subject step refuses a branch, and the predicate check refuses a predicate about another commit. Both runs of assure record exit non-zero, write nothing, and leave the repository with no change.

title: A change under which an obligation falls is refused, and one that only adds unbuilt, unproved obligations passes
when: With a fixture repository whose base head has two invariants built and proved, one only designed and a constraint only designed: assure gate change runs for a change that adds an invariant with no rule and no test, and then for a change that adds it and also removes the rules' file and one test record, each with a passed proof run at its commit.
then: The first change passes with no reason, and the decision gives its coverage. The second exits non-zero and names each obligation that fell with its share: both invariants from built, and one also from proved.

title: A change is not gated when Lathe finds an error in the spec at the base head or at the change
when: assure gate change runs, with a passed proof run, for a change that drops every rule, test record and rules file against a base head whose spec has a dangling test record, and then for a change with that dangling test record against a clean base head.
then: Each run exits 2, prints no decision, and names the error Lathe finds, so a spec with errors is never read as an empty coverage.

title: A change with no verified proof run at its commit, or with an automated test record not passed there, is refused
when: assure gate change runs for one change with a store that keeps no attestation; one forged attestation and one about another commit; a proof run signed at another pull request's ref; a proof run with a failed test and a test with no outcome; one with a skipped test; and one in which every automated test passed.
then: Each run but the last exits non-zero. With no proof run that verifies, the reason says there is no verified proof run at the commit and why each attestation is refused. Otherwise each test record that did not pass is named with its result. The last run passes.

title: A refusal names each obligation that fell with its share and each test record that did not pass, and exits non-zero
when: assure gate change runs, with the job's step summary file set, for a change that removes the rules' file, a test record and an invariant, and whose proof run has the remaining automated test failed. Then it runs, with another step summary file, for a change whose spec has a test record that names a file that does not exist. Then it runs with that summary file set and no --base.
then: It exits non-zero and says the change is refused. The reasons are each on a line of their own: each obligation that fell, with each share it fell from, the invariant the change removes as absent at the change with the share it had at the base, and the failed test record. The step summary holds the same decision, and the repository has no change. For the change with the broken spec it exits 2 and prints no decision, and the other step summary holds one line that says no decision was reached and names Lathe's error. With no --base it exits 2, and the summary holds one line that says no decision was reached because the gate is called wrongly.

title: The same commit, base and proof run give the same decision and reasons in the same order
when: assure gate change runs twice for a change refused for five reasons, with a change-grade proof run and a forged one; then a third time with the store giving the attestations in the other order and with changes in the working tree.
then: The three runs give the same exit code and the same decision, byte for byte.

title: A change is refused for a code-standard fault the base head does not have, and a fault the base has is reported, not refused
when: With a fixture repository whose base head has two code-standard faults, a Go file no record names and a rule record whose identifier its file does not declare, and a passed proof run at each change: assure gate change runs for a change that adds another Go file no record names, for a change that keeps the base's faults, for a change under which the rule record names another identifier its file does not declare, and for a change that removes the unnamed file of the base.
then: The first change exits 1 and names the new file with its rule and key as the one reason; its code faults list all three by rule and key, the new one as not at base and the others as present at base. The second change passes and reports both faults of the base as present at base. The third passes: the fault keeps its rule and key, and is reported with its new reason as present at base. The fourth passes and reports only the fault that remains.

title: A proof run signed at the change's own ref counts only while the workflows folder is the base's, and one signed at main counts for any tree
when: assure gate change runs for a change that alters, adds and removes a workflow file, first with a passed proof run signed at the change's own ref, then with one signed at main; then for a change that leaves the workflows folder as the base has it, with a passed proof run signed at its own ref.
then: The first run is refused: no verified proof run, because the change alters the workflows folder, and each file that differs is named. The second and third runs pass.

title: The gate job builds assure from the base commit only, and runs it in the change's checkout with the pinned Lathe, which the change cannot alter
when: Reads the proof run workflow, its gate job and every key of the job and its steps, and compares the job with the expected job that the test holds. Then, in a fixture repository, assure gate change runs with a Lathe that a run on the change's tree rewrites, so that a run of the rewritten Lathe gives no coverage, for a change that rewrites it and has a passed proof run; then it runs again with the rewritten Lathe.
then: The gate job is exactly the expected job: each key of the job, and each step in order with each of its keys (run, with, env, uses, working-directory, if, shell and any other), so that no text that shell quoting hides can enter it; the workflow runs only on a push to main, a pull request and by hand. In that job: the workflow and the job have no defaults and no key that lets a failed step pass, and the job has no environment of its own; the workflow's environment is only the change's commit and LATHE_REF, a full commit. The job runs on each pull request unless the run is cancelled, may only read the repository, uses only the checkout, setup-go and setup-node actions, and restores no cache. It checks out exactly three things: the change's commit with its full history into stego, Lathe at LATHE_REF, and the pull request's base commit into a folder of its own, with no other input. Each step sets only the environment it needs, by its exact value: the deploy key, workspace mode off for the build, and the base and the token for the gate. The only go command of the job builds assure in the base's cmd/assure, after that checkout, into the runner's temporary folder. No step but the gate runs in or names the change's checkout, runs git, or runs a package manager, an interpreter or a script outside Lathe's folder, and every step before the gate runs. Right before the gate, a step makes Lathe and the built binary read-only. The gate step runs exactly that binary in the change's checkout, for the change's commit against the pull request's base, with one --lathe that names the Lathe built from LATHE_REF, and with only the base and the token in its environment. The first gate run passes, and the change's run did rewrite the Lathe: the base was measured before it. The second run gives no decision, as the rewritten Lathe cannot measure the base.

title: A release is refused while any obligation is not designed, built and proved, and each such obligation is named
when: With a fixture repository and a passed proof run signed at main at each commit: assure gate release runs at a commit whose spec has an obligation Lathe counts as neither built nor proved and one it counts as not proved, and then at a commit whose every obligation is designed, built and proved.
then: The first decision is refused, gives the coverage at the commit, names each obligation with each share it does not have (one not proved, the other not built and not proved), and no decision predicate is written. The fully proved commit passes.
notes: Measures ST-BO07: the share of obligations designed, built and proved is what this gate reads, and a release passes only at 100%.

title: A release commit with no verified proof run, or with an automated test record not passed there, is refused
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved: assure gate release runs with a store that keeps no attestation; with a forged attestation; with a proof run signed at main in which a test failed and one has no outcome; with one in which a test was skipped; and with one in which every automated test passed.
then: Each run but the last exits 1 and writes no predicate. With no proof run that verifies, the reason says there is no verified proof run at the commit and why. Otherwise each test record that did not pass is named with its result. The last run passes.

title: The release gate job runs on a push to main, and only the attest-release job, which runs no repository code, signs a passed decision with the commit as subject
when: Reads proof-run.yml key by key: the workflow, and the gate-release and attest-release jobs with every key of each job and every step with each of its keys and values, in order, against the keys, steps and values allowed. Runs the gate-release job's gate step with an assure that exits 0, 1, 2 and 3. Runs the attest-release job's subject step for a commit and for a branch name, and its predicate check step with a passed release decision about the commit, one about another commit, a refused one, one of the change gate and one with no kind.
then: The workflow has only its allowed keys, read-only permissions and no environment but the commit and the Lathe pin. The gate-release job is exactly: needs the attest job, runs on each push to main also when the suites or the attest job fail, may only read the repository, gives the gate step's output passed as its own, and its ten steps: require the deploy key, check out the commit with its full history and the pinned Lathe, set up Go with no cache and Node, build Lathe, build assure, remove the Go problem matcher, run assure gate release with the commit, a predicate under the runner's temporary folder and the Lathe the workflow builds, and upload the predicate only when passed is true; no other step has a condition or goes on after an error. The gate step gives passed=true for exit 0, ends green with passed=false for a refused release (exit 1), and fails with no output for exit 2 or 3. Every action is pinned to a commit. Only the attest and attest-release jobs may get an identity token or write attestations. The attest-release job is exactly: needs the gate-release job and runs only when its output passed is true, may only get an identity token and write attestations, has no container or defaults, and its four steps: download the predicate, check it, name the commit as the subject, and sign it with actions/attest at the release-decision predicate type; it checks out and runs no code of the repository. The subject step names the commit as the subject with the SHA-256 of its ID as the digest and refuses the branch, and the check accepts only the passed release decision about the commit.

title: A release commit whose tree has a code-standard fault is refused, and each fault is named with its file and rule
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved, and a passed proof run signed at main: assure gate release runs at a commit that adds a Go file no record names and names, in a rule record, an identifier that the rule's file does not declare.
then: It exits 1 and writes no predicate. The decision gives a coverage of 100% for each share, lists both faults in its code faults with the file and the rule, ST-STD-CODE-R02 before ST-STD-CODE-R05, and names each as a reason with its file, the rule and its key.

title: A release takes only a proof run signed at main, and one signed at any other ref is refused with the ref named
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved: assure gate release runs with a passed proof run signed at a pull request's ref, then with one signed at another branch, then with both one signed at the pull request's ref and one signed at main.
then: The first two runs exit 1, write no predicate, and say that there is no verified proof run at the commit because the attestation is signed at that ref, not at refs/heads/main. The third run passes, and its decision rests on the proof run signed at main.

title: The ledger comes from verified attestations and the committed spec, and no file of the working tree changes it
when: With a fixture repository of five commits and a store that keeps proof run attestations for four of them, one of which fails verification: assure ledger runs for the newest commit with a clean tree; then with the working tree at the oldest commit, its spec changed and evidence files that say every test passed; then with a store that keeps no attestation; then for a commit with no spec, with a short commit ID, with no commit and with a depth of zero.
then: The first two runs print the same ledger, byte for byte, from the committed spec and the verified attestations, and the repository has no change. With no attestation every result is none, no test record has passed, and it exits 1. The commit with no spec and the wrong calls exit 2 and print no ledger.

title: Each test record shows its state, its result at the commit and the newest commit a verified proof run passed it at, within the depth
when: With a fixture repository of five commits whose newest has a proof run with one automated test failed, the next none, the next one that fails verification and the next both automated tests passed: assure ledger runs for the newest commit twice, then with --depth 2, then for a commit whose proof run passed every test, then with a store in which a test never passed.
then: Each line gives the test record, its state, its result at the commit and the newest commit it passed at; the walk passes over the commit with no attestation, asks for each commit once, and stops where every automated test has passed. The two runs give the same text. With --depth 2 the failed test says not within 2 commits. When every automated test passed it exits 0 and lists only the manual test as not passed; otherwise it exits 1. A test that never passed makes the walk reach the root commit.

title: An attestation that fails verification gives no result at its commit, and the ledger says why
when: With the history of ST-ASR-UC04-R02-T01 and the attestation at the newest commit forged: assure ledger runs for that commit. Then, with change-grade proof runs signed at a pull request's ref: it runs for a change, without and with GITHUB_REF set to that ref; for a commit made as a pull request's merge ref, whose first parent is main's head, with a change-grade attestation, one signed at main by a run at another commit and one signed at a branch at commit 4; for a change that alters a workflow file; and with --base or --main naming the commit itself (the reviewer's spoof).
then: An attestation that is unverifiable or change grade shows as none, with the reason. At the forged commit every result is none, the proof run line says none is verified at release grade, and a line for that commit and one for the forged ancestor give the verifier's reason; the passes come from the older verified proof run, and it exits 1. Each change-grade attestation, at the commit or at an ancestor, is listed as change grade at its ref, counting only in its own gate, and gives no result, with GITHUB_REF set or not; it exits 1. For the merge ref the last passes come from the release-grade proof runs of its first-parent history, and the attestation signed at main by a run at another commit and the one at a branch are refused with their reasons. --base and --main are not flags of assure ledger: it exits 2 and prints no ledger.

title: A failed resolution leaves go.mod and go.sum as they were
when: With a project with applied code, go.mod and go.sum, and a fake go runner: Resolution fails in each of nine ways, from a failing go command to a file edited during the run.
then: go.mod and go.sum keep their bytes, and no transaction file is left.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. it covers the failed run, not the interrupted one.

title: An interrupted resolution is recoverable
when: With a project with applied code, and the local Go SDK: Resolution is interrupted after its first journal operation, then compiler.Recover runs, then a fresh resolution.
then: The interrupted run reports that recovery is required; recovery and the fresh resolution succeed; the record claims neither module file.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. one interruption point only, through compiler.Recover rather than the stego recover command, and it does not check that both files are exactly the old or the new version after recovery.

title: A saved overlay flag and ambient GOFLAGS cannot change what resolution reads
when: With a project with a Go configuration file that saves a -overlay flag, and an invalid ambient GOFLAGS: Resolution runs offline.
then: The overlay's import never reaches go.mod, and the source is unchanged.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today.

title: Resolution ignores an ambient vendor flag and a missing go.work
when: With a project with a local replace directive, GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor and GOWORK naming a missing file, with GOPROXY off: Resolution runs twice.
then: Both runs succeed, give the same go.mod, and keep the local replacement.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today.

title: Resolution refuses a project that was never applied and names apply
when: With a project whose code was never applied: Resolution runs.
then: It fails, and the error names stego apply.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. the stale case, where the declaration changed after apply, is not exercised.

title: The build environment drops ambient settings and sets GOPROXY off
when: With an environment with GOFLAGS, GOWORK, GOENV, GOCACHEPROG, LD_PRELOAD, GH_TOKEN and HTTPS_PROXY set: The build environment is derived.
then: None of those settings remain, and GOPROXY is off.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. GOPROXY=off stops module fetches only; no build runs with the network off, and no build fails on a missing or mismatched cached module.

title: An offline record names a cache and no proxy, and an online record names no cache
when: With a valid offline build record and a valid online one: Each is changed so that its proxy and cache disagree.
then: validateRecord refuses each.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. see ST-BLD-INV04-T.

title: A record whose SDK digest differs is refused
when: With a valid build record: Its toolchain digest is changed.
then: validateRecord refuses it.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. the archetype's pin is not built; the record is checked against the compiler's SDK.

title: A build refuses an SDK that is not the verified one
when: With build options naming a fake go binary: Build runs.
then: It refuses the SDK and writes no work directory.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. see ST-BLD-INV05-T.

title: A record of one build is refused
when: With a valid build record: Its independent build count is set to one.
then: validateRecord refuses it.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. no test builds twice and compares bytes, or fails on a difference. TestCommandRejectsOutputLimitAndCancellation shows only that the two builds get different environments.

title: A record whose inputs, modules or build settings changed is refused
when: With a valid build record: One input, module or build setting changes.
then: validateRecord refuses each.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. see ST-BLD-INV07-T.

title: The module inventory names each module once with no host path
when: With a module list with a local replacement, a repeated module and a malformed h1: sum: The module inventory is built.
then: The local replacement is recorded as common with no host path; the repeated module and the malformed sum are refused.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. one part of the record only.

title: A record whose canonical bytes do not hash to the trusted digest is refused
when: With a build record on disk: Verify runs with a wrong digest, then with a non-canonical record.
then: Both are refused.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. the digest is a plain argument; no test joins it to verified provenance. In CI, scripts/test_application_records.py shows the attestation checks run before any output.

title: A source check refuses an untrusted record digest
when: With a source snapshot and its record: VerifySource runs with a wrong digest, and with an empty, file, symlinked or missing root.
then: Each is refused.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. see ST-BLD-UC04-R01-T01.

title: A source snapshot is refused on any changed, missing or added file
when: With a source snapshot that matches its record: One file's content, mode or presence changes, a file is added, a symlink appears, or .git metadata appears.
then: Each is refused.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. each check stops at the first difference and names only that one; the requirement asks for every difference. That is a code gap in appbuild.Verify, VerifySource and VerifyImage.

title: An image is refused when any digest its record names differs
when: With an image layout and its record: The executable or the CA bundle differs from the record.
then: VerifyImage refuses it.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. it verifies an image; it does not show image build refusing an executable no trusted build record names, nor that the host's trust store is never read.

title: The same build gives the same image, running as non-root
when: With one executable and one CA bundle: The image is assembled twice.
then: Equal records and layout digests; the config runs as user 65532.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. the scratch base is not asserted directly, and the test calls assembleImage rather than the command.

title: A rehashed image that runs as root or carries an extra executable is refused
when: With an image whose descriptors are correctly rehashed after a change: It runs as root, carries an ambient env value, a writable or symlinked executable, an extra executable, or a private key in its trust store.
then: VerifyImage refuses each.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. it proves the verifier, not that image build never produces such an image.

title: Both records are checked against the exact signer identity before any output exists
when: With a consumer policy and a mocked gh: The record check runs.
then: Each record is checked against the exact identity, before any output exists.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. see ST-BLD-INV10-T.

title: The reusable workflow signer is pinned by digest and workflow, with no identity regex
when: With a reusable-workflow policy and a mocked gh: The record check runs.
then: Each record is checked with the signer digest and workflow, and no identity regex or signer repository selector is used.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. see ST-BLD-INV10-T.

title: A push over TLS with an explicit CA reads back the exact image
when: With an in-process TLS registry with basic auth, an explicit CA, and HTTPS_PROXY set: A verified image is pushed and then retrieved; the source is edited after capture.
then: The retrieved bytes equal the captured layout, the proxy is ignored, and the later edit changes nothing.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. the push is a direct remote.Write, not PublishImage, so PublishImage refusing an unverified image and its read-back refusing different bytes are not exercised.

title: An exported image archive is the same bytes each time and never overwrites
when: With a verified image layout: It is exported twice; then with an existing output; then with a changed config blob.
then: The two archives are equal; the existing output is kept; the changed blob is refused and nothing is written.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. export only.

title: Publication refuses a wrong CA, a bad credential file or a tagged repository
when: With an in-process TLS registry: The CA digest differs, the CA is untrusted, the credential file has a wrong mode, is a link, has extra fields or is missing, the token origin is http, the origins overlap, or the repository carries a tag.
then: Each is refused before anything is pushed.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. see ST-BLD-UC06-R01-T01.

title: A retrieved image whose bytes differ is refused
when: With an in-process TLS registry that returns changed bytes: The image is retrieved; publish and retrieve are also cancelled.
then: The changed bytes are refused as differing, and cancellation is kept.
notes: Not proof yet: a use case test runs at the level the use case is stated, through the stego command; this test runs in-package today. the trusted build record check and the signature check before writing are not exercised; signature checking is not built.

title: A scaffold refuses to overwrite an existing path
when: With a project directory where the service file, the config file, the state directory or the fills directory already exists as a file, a directory, a symbolic link or a dangling link: scaffold a new project into it.
then: The scaffold refuses, the existing file keeps its content, and the directory the link points to is unchanged.
notes: Not proof yet: this test calls the compiler in process. It is recorded at system, the level the use case is stated at, and counts once a test runs the stego command end to end.

title: Checking a declaration writes nothing
when: With a project whose declaration carries a field with an empty length range, an existing output file and a state file: run the validate, plan and apply commands.
then: Each command fails with a validation error, the existing files keep their content, and no module file is written.

title: A refusal reports every fault at once
when: With a declaration that carries four faults at once, an unknown field type, an enum with no values, a collection with an undeclared entity and an unknown operation: validate it.
then: The check reports at least four faults, and one fault for each of the four.
notes: Not proof yet: this test calls the compiler in process. It is recorded at system, the level the use case is stated at, and counts once a test runs the stego command end to end.

title: Generation refuses only what checking refuses
when: With a declaration that fails one semantic check, such as an empty length range, a bad pattern, an unknown field type or a patchable field that does not exist, and generators that fail the test if they run: validate it, then reconcile it.
then: Validation reports the fault, reconciliation refuses with the same validation report, no generator runs, and no output, module file or state is written.
notes: Not proof yet: this test calls the compiler in process. It is recorded at system, the level the use case is stated at, and counts once a test runs the stego command end to end.

title: Verification fails when the release tag points at another commit
when: With a qualified commit and a published release tag: The tag points at another commit and release verification runs.
then: Qualification fails.

title: Release verification fails when a release signature names another signed artifact run
